newsitem.title: USA: Two triple murderers executed in United States.
newsitem.headline: Two triple murderers executed in United States.

text.p: Two triple murderers were executed by lethal injection in the United States on Friday, one in South Carolina while the other became the first inmate in Oregon to die at the hands of that state in 34 years.

Douglas Wright, 56, was pronounced dead at 12:16 a.m./3:16 a.m. EDT (0717 GMT) for luring homeless people in Portland off the streets in 1991 and killing them in the wilderness. The last person executed in Oregon was LeeRoy McGahuey who died in the gas chamber in 1962.
Wright's execution came hours after another triple-murderer, Michael Torrence, 35, was put to death by lethal injection in South Carolina.
Before his execution, Wright issued a statement of remorse for the death of a 10-year-old Portland boy he claimed to have abducted and killed in 1984.

Wright was sentenced to death in 1993 for the slayings two years earlier of Anthony Barker, William Davis and William Marks, whose bodies were found on the Warm Springs Indian reservation in central Oregon.

Although others have been on the Oregon's Death Row far longer than Wright, the Iowa native declined to fight his sentence, saying he deserved to die after a life of crime that included a previous prison term for a double-homicide.

In his statement, read to reporters by state prison director Dave Cook, Wright said he could no longer live with "my guilt, my personal shame nor my unbearable grief" for 10-year-old Luke Treadway, whose disappearance has never been solved.
Wright said last week he was responsible for the boy's molestation and death, but he was unable to lead detectives to the body.

Prison officials said Wright expressed relief late Thursday when he learned the Oregon Supreme Court had rejected an eleventh-hour appeal filed over his objections by the American Civil Liberties Union.
Wright's final meal was a farmhand's breakfast of five fried eggs, crispy bacon, hash-brown potatoes, pancakes, coffee, orange juice and milk.

In the Broad River Correctional Institution in Columbia, S.C., Torrence, a sixth-grade dropout who also said he wanted to die, downed a last meal of steak, shrimp and lobster prepared by a Japanese restaurant before his execution.

Torrence was convicted in the February 1987 deaths of millworkers Dennis Lollis and Charles Bush during a robbery. A month later, he shot Charleston prostitute Cynthia Williams and dumped her body along a highway.
He had petitioned the South Carolina Supreme Court since 1994 to let him drop his appeals.
Just before the execution, Torrence said in a brief statement read by his lawyer that he "understands an apology is not sufficient, but hopes his understanding gives them some comfort."
Torrence died at 1:21 a.m. EDT, prisons spokesman John Barkley said. Torrence was the third person executed in South Carolina this year.
